mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 1.0%) compresses discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS < 1.0% for 3 consecutive months but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of such periods over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A falling unemployment rate (UNRATE < 5.0%) signals a tightening labor market, boosting consumer spending and corporate earnings, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE < 5.0%, S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is low (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) and inflation is high (CPIAUCSL > 2.5%), the market perceives a 'higher for longer' rate environment, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: In periods where FEDFUNDS < 0.5% and CPIAUCSL > 2.5%, S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 1,100,000 units annually and the economy is in expansion (UNRATE < 5.5%), strong consumer confidence drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: In periods where UNRATE < 5.5% and HOUST > 1,100,000, S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 100.0) signals an economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO < 100.0, S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A strong labor market (PAYEMS growth > 0.5% year-over-year) consistently drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In any 3-year rolling window, the Rank IC for PAYEMS as a predictor of 20-day returns is less than 0.03, or the positive return rate when PAYEMS growth > 0.5% is below 55%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS > 0.3% growth) and decline in unemployment (UNRATE falls > 0.2pp) signal a robust labor market, boosting consumer spending and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: In periods where PAYEMS growth > 0.3% and UNRATE falls > 0.2pp, S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in retail sales (RSAFS < 400000) signals weak consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When RSAFS < 400000, S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.
